clue.text: Is she worried by French driver's glass eye?

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so the driver comes next to the other piece

parts.note: Alain Prost is a French Formula One champion

indicators.note: worried means agitated, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frets whether a French racing driver's wife will mind his false eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a glass eye as one example of an artificial body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosthesis is an artificial body part, and a glass eye is one kind.

clue.text: Bank without any charges putting foot down

indicators.note: Putting something down sends it to the bottom, and the bottom of a down entry is its last letter, so the f that stands for foot travels there and the rest closes up above it.

parts.note: what costs nothing to use is free

explanation.surface: A bank that takes no fees, and a driver flooring the accelerator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting foot down' reads as flooring the accelerator and is an instruction about a letter, f being the surveyor's foot. The bank wanted is the kind a ship runs aground on.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or coral lying just under the sea, a bank in the sandbank sense rather than the money one.

clue.text: Mao and Stalin worked out an end to Channel crossings

indicators.note: A problem worked out has had its parts shifted around until they make sense, and that is what happens to these letters.

parts.note: the Chinese chairman, three letters for the mixture
the Soviet leader supplies the other six

explanation.surface: Two dictators sitting down together to negotiate an end to cross-Channel traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An end to' offers itself as an instruction to drop a final letter, and it is the far end of a journey. Saint-Malo is the walled Breton port where the ferries from southern England tie up.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint-Malo is the Brittany port a Channel ferry from England berths in, so the crossing ends there.

clue.text: Stop mad bishop getting into barrel for Easter tradition

indicators.note: What gets into a thing ends up surrounded by it, so the letters named before this go inside the barrel named after it.

parts.note: ho! is the old cry meaning hold, halt there
a tun is the largest cask a brewer keeps
cross is the everyday British word for angry
b is the bishop on a chess scoresheet

explanation.surface: A shout to head off a furious bishop as he climbs into a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ho!' is the old cry meaning halt, and a tun is a brewer's cask; both are older words than the surface lets on. The bishop keeps the sentence in church while handing over the letter a chess player writes for him.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot cross buns are the spiced buns marked with a pastry cross that Britain eats at Easter, sold from Good Friday.

clue.text: Car frequently breaks down

indicators.note: Something that breaks into a word forces its way between the letters, so the piece named just before it lands inside the other.

parts.note: Down! is the order that stops a dog where it stands
oft is the poet's word for often

explanation.surface: An unreliable car forever going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks down' reads as one phrase about a car that will not start, and its two words do separate jobs, the second being an order shouted at a dog. 'Breaks' invites an anagram; it is an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft top is a convertible, named for the folding fabric roof, so 'car' names it by its kind.

clue.text: These egg boxes detect surroundings

indicators.note: To box something is to shut it in, so the words in front of this one have the letters shut away inside them.

parts.note: three letters in a row, running across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Egg cartons clever enough to sense what is around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' is the verb and not the cartons, which is the whole of the disguise. Short answers hide in the smallest spans, and this one straddles a word break where the eye slides past it.
explanation.definitionFit: To see is to take in what lies around you, so detecting your surroundings is the eye's whole job.

clue.text: Avoid rear-end collision when Tesla moves off

indicators.note: A car that moves off leaves the spot it was standing in, and so does the letter named just before.

parts.note: a shunt is British drivers' slang for a bump from behind
the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density, has the symbol t

explanation.surface: Keeping clear of the car behind when the electric one in front pulls away.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface parks you at a set of traffic lights so that Tesla reads as the car. He is here as Nikola Tesla, the engineer whose name was given to the measure of magnetic field strength.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun a thing is to keep well clear of it, which is what avoiding it amounts to.

clue.text: Fight with spades and manure

parts.note: s is the card player's spades
crap is the coarse word for dung

explanation.surface: A brawl fought with garden spades and handfuls of muck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spades' is the card suit rather than the garden tool, which is what keeps the surface outdoors. The letter comes from bridge and whist scoring, where each suit is written as its initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a short untidy fight, the playground word rather than the military one.

clue.text: Play down south of Texas, say

parts.note: south is the foot of any map, so to be south of a place is to be under it
Texas is one of fifty, and 'say' asks for the class it belongs to

explanation.surface: Putting on a play somewhere below the Texas border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down south' wants to be a region, and the definition stops at 'down'. A comma followed by 'say' nearly always means you are being handed an example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To understate something is to play it down, presenting it as smaller or milder than it really is.

clue.text: Cricket boundaries rolled back for test, favouring beefier types?

indicators.note: Something rolled back runs the other way, and an across entry going the other way is read from its right-hand end.

parts.note: a ball hit clear of the field is a six, and the plural is then run backwards
t stands for test

explanation.surface: The ropes brought in before a Test match, to the benefit of the bigger hitters.
explanation.walkthrough: Boundaries in cricket are the sixes and fours a batter scores, not the rope round the field, which is the step the surface hides. The question mark admits the definition is a joke about muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexist rates one sex above the other, and the beefier of the two is the one the word is usually accused of favouring.

clue.text: Some sponging as Mexican beans are cooked for Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two parts trade their first sounds

parts.note: Mexican beans are refried, cooked again; re- means again, said ree
fried is a way of cooking, said fride

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism on refried beans, the mashed Mexican staple.
explanation.walkthrough: Say RE-FRIED and swap its opening sounds R and FR to hear FREE RIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A free ride is a benefit got without paying, which is what sponging off others means.

clue.text: Migrant protestor catches old marines assaulting Nazi

indicators.note: A migrant does not stay put, and neither do these letters, which settle somewhere other than where they started.
What the protestor catches is taken in, so the letters named next join the mixture instead of standing apart from it.

parts.note: nine letters for the mixture
o is the standard short form of old
RM is the Royal Marines, Britain's seaborne commando force

explanation.surface: A demonstrator about migration grabbing hold of old marines as they set about a Nazi.
explanation.walkthrough: The mixture swallows more than it looks, since two abbreviations are caught up among the protestor's letters. Sturmabteilung, the party militia being named, translates as assault detachment.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi party's Sturmabteilung was its assault detachment, so its brownshirted members were Nazis whose trade was the attack.

clue.text: Revered old novelist heard cheers wandering into exhibition

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the sound of the name rather than its spelling

parts.note: Jane Austen, the much-loved novelist of the early 1800s
TA is informal British for thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: wandering means straying from place to place, so the letters of into move around

explanation.surface: Someone hears cheers for a great writer while drifting into a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist is Jane Austen, and 'heard' asks only for the sound of her name, spelt here as it is said in the answer's opening. TA is British slang for thanks; 'wandering' scrambles the word into.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostentation is a showy display meant to impress, which is what exhibition means in the sense of showing off.

clue.text: Saint shut up as church wasted power

parts.note: s is the short form of saint, as in S Paul
pent means penned in, as in pent-up feelings
as and for both mean because when they join two statements
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A saint silenced because the church squandered its authority.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on as part of the same sentence, which is how the join hides. 'As' meaning 'for' is the old causal sense: he stayed indoors, as it was raining.
explanation.definitionFit: A spent force is a person or movement whose power is used up, still present but no longer able to make anything happen.

clue.text: Max caught by cat swung round makes feelings clear

indicators.note: Whatever is caught is held inside the thing that caught it, so these letters are written within the other piece.
Swing a thing round and it faces the other way, so the cat's letters are set down from the back.

parts.note: puss is the nursery name for a cat, and the four letters are then set down backwards
the max of anything is its peak

explanation.surface: A cat whirling about with somebody called Max in its teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Max' is the short form of maximum, not the man the surface invents. An across entry turned round is read right to left, which is all 'swung round' is asking for.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak up is to say plainly what you think, which is how feelings get made clear.

clue.text: Age stomach's beginning to go from drinking a lot

indicators.note: The beginning of a word is the letter it starts with, and no more of it than that.

parts.note: somebody drinking a lot is thirsty

indicators.note: What goes from a word has left it, so the letter named is the one taken out of the longer word.

parts.note: the letter the word stomach starts with

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker whose stomach is starting to give out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Age' is the whole definition, though it reads as the first word of a sentence about a drinker's decline. English gives ages as bare numbers, which is what lets a number answer to the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirty is an age, the bare number English uses when somebody is asked how old they are.

clue.text: "I'm stinking and hot" — an imprisoned ex-PM

parts.note: the clue's own two letters, with the apostrophe dropped
a rank smell is a stinking one
h is the letter on a hot tap
the clue's own word, taken as it stands

explanation.surface: Somebody complaining about their own smell and the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks do surface work only: the words inside them supply letters rather than speech. Imran Khan captained Pakistan to the 1992 cricket World Cup long before he governed it.
explanation.definitionFit: Imran Khan was Pakistan's prime minister until 2022 and has been held in jail since 2023, which is what an imprisoned ex-PM is.

clue.text: Cryptic note by doctor put with dead bodies

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling or hidden in meaning, so the letters of note are presented in a disguised order

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor's puzzling note is placed alongside corpses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' looks like a description of the doctor's handwriting, but it tells you to rearrange the word note. MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is the usual crossword doctor alongside DR and GP.
explanation.definitionFit: To entomb is to place in a tomb, where the dead are laid to rest.

clue.text: Miss one stair, taking a tumble

indicators.note: Anything that takes a tumble ends up in a heap, its parts no longer in the order they were in.

parts.note: eight letters for the mixture

explanation.surface: Missing a step and going headlong down the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' is the title and not the verb the fall wants, and it is the only word of the clue standing outside the mixture. The accent Spanish puts over the n is dropped, since grids have no room for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Senorita is the Spanish title for an unmarried woman, used where English says Miss.

clue.text: Outsiders in Surrey wrongly took bloody beating

indicators.note: The outsiders of a word are the letters standing at each end of it, with everything between them left behind.

parts.note: the first and last letters of the English county's name
to take a thing wrongly is to steal it, and the past tense is wanted

explanation.surface: Outlying parts of Surrey taking a violent beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' sits exactly where an anagram indicator would sit and does none of that work, since taking wrongly is stealing. 'Bloody' is literal: the beat in question is the heart's.
explanation.definitionFit: Systole is the phase of the heartbeat in which the heart contracts and drives blood out, so the beating really is bloody.

clue.text: Among others, world champions heading for seaside as reward

parts.note: 'I, for one' picks a single instance out of a group, which is the job among others does
Spain's footballers are world champions, the women's side having taken the title in 2023

indicators.note: The heading of a word is the letter at its top, so only the first letter of the word after this is taken.

parts.note: the letter the word seaside starts with

explanation.surface: The world's best team heading for the coast to collect their prize.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces cut straight across the answer's own words, so the joins are nowhere near where the spaces fall. 'Among others' is the idiom buried in 'I, for one'.
explanation.definitionFit: What you get for your pains is what your effort earned you, said almost always of a reward that turns out to be nothing of the kind.

clue.text: Romantic gift went up Charles's backside

definitions.note: A bunch of roses is one gift, so the singular noun of the definition covers a plural answer.

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise

indicators.note: The backside of a name is the end of it, so its final letter is all that is taken.

parts.note: the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: A bouquet disappearing up Charles's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went up' in a down clue offers itself as a reversal and is only the past tense of rise. Charles is here for his final letter, and for the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Roses are the flowers sent on Valentine's Day, the standard romantic gift.

clue.text: One egg you should sit on

indicators.note: Whatever sits on a thing is above it, and above in a down entry means earlier, so this letter is written over the egg.

parts.note: u is 'you' in a text message
a nit is the egg a head louse lays

explanation.surface: A hen being told which single egg to brood.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is of brooding and the instruction is about position, since in a down entry what sits on a thing is written above it. Texting supplies the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single one of whatever is being counted, so the bare word one covers it.

clue.text: What appears to be bubbly text copied to Oscar

parts.note: prose is ordinary written text, as against verse
cc on a memo or an email marks who was copied in, from carbon copy
Oscar is o in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A cheerful message copied on to somebody called Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' is the party word for champagne, and the definition hedges because this is the Italian sparkler poured instead. 'Text' is written matter, not a message on a phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubbly is the nickname for champagne, and prosecco is the Italian sparkling wine that stands in for it.

clue.text: What might be serious for patient wanting A&E?

definitions.text: What might be serious for patient wanting A&E?

indicators.note: What a thing wants is what it lacks, so the letters named here are the ones missing from the word.

parts.note: an acute condition is a serious one
A&E is the British hospital's accident and emergency department, and its two letters are the ones taken out

explanation.surface: A wound bad enough to send somebody to casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word works twice, describing the injury and naming the two letters to drop, which is what &lit means. The question mark is there because a cut is only one of the things that might be serious.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: a cut is the sort of thing that might be serious enough to send a patient to casualty.

clue.text: Patents, trademarks etc. perfect for high-tech brand

parts.note: IP is intellectual property, the law that covers patents and trademarks
to hone a thing is to perfect it, sharpening it by degrees

explanation.surface: A portfolio of patents and trademarks, ideal for a technology company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' reads as an adjective in the surface and is a verb in the wordplay, which is the whole of the disguise. Apple's lower-case i has been the house prefix since the iMac.
explanation.definitionFit: The iPhone is Apple's smartphone, a brand name that stands for high technology.

clue.text: Pickle Anne gets out of cruelty

indicators.note: Whoever gets out of a place is no longer inside it, so this name's letters leave the longer word.

parts.note: meanness is cruelty of the small, unkind sort
the four letters that leave, together and in that order

explanation.surface: Anne getting herself out of somebody's unkindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pickle' is the fix you find yourself in rather than the jar, and it is the definition sitting first. The name comes out in one continuous run, which is what makes the gap findable.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickle is a predicament, and being in a pickle is being in a mess, the two words used the same way.

clue.text: Confuse Asian visiting Nottinghamshire for audition

indicators.note: An audition is judged by ear, so these words are wanted for the sound they make and not for the way they are spelt.

parts.note: a Thai is an Asian, and the name is said like the thing worn with a collar
somebody visiting a county is in it
Notts is how the English county is written short, and the word it sounds like begins with a silent k

explanation.surface: Putting off an Asian visitor to Nottinghamshire who has come for an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: Three scraps of sound are stitched together and then respelt, so the spaces in the answer fall nowhere near the joins in the clue. Notts is what the county is called on an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie someone in knots is to leave them thoroughly confused, unable to follow their own argument.
